subject: science
passage: Water fleas of the genus Daphnia often reproduce without mating, so a single female can give rise to a large clone of genetically identical offspring. When young members of some clones develop in water containing chemicals released by predatory insect larvae, they grow pointed helmets and spines that make them harder to swallow; their identical sisters raised in predator-free water grow no such defenses. ______ one set of genes can yield either a defended or an undefended body, depending on the chemical surroundings in which an individual develops.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence describes genetically identical sisters that grow different bodies in different water. The last sentence states the general meaning of that observation in plainer terms: the same genes can produce either body type, depending on the environment. A restatement transition fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a new case that resembles the previous one, but the last sentence describes the same water fleas, not a parallel case. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "For instance" introduces an example, but the last sentence is a general statement; the specific example came in the sentence before it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the last sentence agrees with and sums up the previous sentence.
explanation.D: Correct. "In other words" signals that the last sentence restates the observation about identical sisters as a general point about genes and environment.
